analysis.title: Fireworks Day: Stocks Fawke'd, AI/Tech Wrecked On "Massive Retail Selling"; Bonds & Bullion Bid
key_insights: US equities sold off hard at the cash open on Nov 5 (note dated Nov 6). NDX fell below election-night lows, down over 5% from the pre-election close, and back below its 200DMA for the first time since April. SPX fell toward its 200DMA.

Every SPX sector closed red. Tech fell around 7%. The SOX fell nearly 10% in a day, comparable to the Broadcom fallout in June and Liberation Day. NVDA fell 9% and is negative YTD. QCOM and ARM dropped after earnings.
The note names the catalyst as political. Democrats swept both chambers in the midterms, which raised fears of limits on AI spending and data center buildouts.
The broad AI basket is down about 12% from pre-election levels while SPX ex-AI is still holding gains. NeoClouds are down about 20% since the election.

Goldman's equity desk (John Flood) reports that long-only investors are frozen and hedge funds sold hyperscalers they bought the day before. Retail-heavy brokers report a second day of notable sell skews. Volumes versus the 20-day average: SPY +160%, QQQ +100%, SMH +150%, DRAM +75%.

Goldman's desk sees the semis pressure as a data center capacity argument. Land, power and shell bottlenecks from permitting may mean 2028 gigawatts added are near flat y/y with 2027, against the >30% y/y growth investors expected. That would leave too many semiconductors for the available data center shells. Memory names (HDD, DRAM, NAND), E&C stocks, IPPs/power with TX, GA and OH exposure, and neoclouds are also under pressure.

Goldman Prime Brokerage reports TMT severely down on Nov 5, US-focused fundamental funds hit harder, and multi-strategy funds down significantly on equity exposure. Systematic funds were positive. On Nov 4, a semis-to-software rotation drove a sharp momentum sell-off.

UBS says retail market-making clients sold at the 0.5th percentile versus 3 years this morning, then turned to buying after 11:15 NY. UBS expects retail may sell more Friday and that risk-control funds will sell systematically, likely over $100bn. UBS does not think the low is in, and says Monday's pre-open could be the low, as in August 2024 and April 2025.

Vanda Research reports the largest 30-minute retail selling episode in single stocks since October, on track to be the largest retail selling since the late-July capitulation. Vanda says retail selling continued for days last time and suggests watching for institutional buying to start a recovery.

Analyst views are split. Wedbush's Dan Ives reportedly sees another 10-12% downside for chips. Fundstrat's Tom Lee calls the AI selloff an overreaction and predicts a 20% tech rally. Nomura's McElligott says negative gamma is large. Goldman's Privorotsky says nets are too low for the broader market to go down easily.

VIX rose to its highest since early April. NDX vol trades at a wide premium to SPX vol. The note estimates a $2.8 trillion one-day loss in market value, the largest ever, and says Musk's companies have lost a combined $460bn since the election.
Data-center CDS spreads rose above 500bps, a record. CRWV bond spreads topped 1200bps. Hyperscaler CDS widened modestly and IG spreads rose more notably. AI capex funding costs hit a record high.

Treasuries rallied as the main safe haven. The 2Y yield is down 17bps since before the election and the 30Y is down 8bps, so the curve bull-steepened. Dec Fed hike odds are 65%, and 2027 pricing no longer includes even one hike. Demand for 10-year calls was reported by Bloomberg.

The note gives the macro driver of the bond bid as fiscal: a Democratic Congress against a Republican White House implies gridlock and less Treasury supply. BofA now expects coupon auction size increases to be delayed until November rather than August, citing debt ceiling dynamics that push the X-date as early as August 2027. South Korea is reportedly weighing large purchases of long-term Treasuries.
Cleveland Fed's Hammack reiterated a hawkish baseline in Zurich, saying policy needs to be restrictive to bring inflation to 2% and preferring smaller, more frequent adjustments.

Crude rebounded from a roughly 9% selloff after Tuesday's election. WTI is near $91 and Brent near $98. Traders called the bounce technical, at the 100/200DMAs. The selloff reflected bets that a Democratic Congress would speed an end to the Iran war, and Hormuz flows have recovered to near pre-war levels.

Brent CFDs flipped into contango for the first time since mid-July. Aramco cut its December Arab Light OSP to Asia by $2/bbl, to $7 below the regional benchmark, the lowest in six years. Vitol bought Forties from Trafigura at about a $4 discount to Dated Brent. The note concludes physical supply is comfortable. Ukraine struck Russia's 340,000 b/d Ryazan refinery.
JPY was bid and the dollar gained. Gold was bid overnight but sold in the US session on liquidity needs. Bitcoin gave back the prior day's gains and fell to about $75K.

BTIG's Krinsky has a benign base case (semis find a floor, defensives cool, rotation flips). He flags the bad case: semis broke July lows, Japan chips are in freefall, healthcare (XLV) is at a record 19% above its 200DMA, and Goldman's CTA model sees $164bn of S&P supply in a down tape after a major vol crush. He calls this the condition for a correlation-one selloff.

The note's own view is that the rotation story explained why the S&P went nowhere for three months. It doubts where the next wave of defensive buying comes from, and cites April 1999 as a case where a 9% dip preceded a final melt-up. It treats that outcome as less likely this time. Payrolls are due the next day.

market_movers.rationale: NVDA fell 9% on the day and is now negative YTD, as semis led the AI/tech selloff.
QCOM dropped after earnings during the semis selloff.
ARM dropped after earnings during the semis selloff.
CRWV bond spreads topped 1200bps as neocloud and data-center credit widened.

sector_views.rationale: Tech fell about 7% and the SOX nearly 10% in one day. Goldman's desk cites a possible excess of chips relative to data center shells by 2028. Ives sees 10-12% more downside for chips, while Lee expects a 20% tech rally.
Staples (-0.5%), Utilities (-0.9%) and Energy (-1.1%) held up better than the market. The note calls the safe-haven rotation visible but modest.
XLV is a record 19% above its 200DMA, which the note says leaves it unclear where further defensive buying comes from.

earnings_insights: QCOM and ARM dropped after their earnings reports during the Nov 5 session. The note gives no EPS or revenue figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Market-implied odds fell on the day as Treasuries rallied. January odds are also falling.
